proposal.title: IBM Cloud support assistant qualification architecture
proposal.body: Adds the complete support workflow using concrete IBM service candidates, preserving the CRM and source systems outside provisioning scope. A single Code Engine application owns the staff interface, source adapters, authorization checks, field filtering, retrieval, drafting, escalation and approved ticket-update processing. These are application modules, not separate provisioned services. Region, model, identity integration, service availability and account access remain unverified; no regional availability or recovery target is assumed. All IBM resources are design-only: this workload needs application code, native infrastructure generation and integration engineering beyond current typed export coverage. First proposed local test: run the application harness against synthetic tickets, CRM records, approved knowledge and identity claims spanning separate tenants and customers. Attempt cross-boundary retrieval, inject sensitive fields and malicious source instructions, request unsupported promises, then approve and replay a ticket update with the same idempotency key. Check denied access, filtered model requests, approved-source citations, escalation, one effective update and matching audit records. Simulate an interrupted update and verify reconciliation before retrying. Scripted model responses exercise control paths only; a separate evaluation with the selected real model must measure grounding, citation accuracy, abstention and unsafe promises. No tests have run, and no artifact-bound emulation evidence exists.

data.label: Support staff
data.description: Existing people using a browser outside provisioning scope. Review cited drafts, handle escalations and explicitly approve ticket updates.

data.label: Staff authentication
data.description: Proposed IBM Cloud App ID for staff authentication. Company sign-in federation and current service availability require verification. Trusted server-side mappings supply staff, tenant and customer permissions; browser claims alone cannot grant access.

data.label: Support application and staff interface
data.description: One Code Engine application serves HTTPS UI/API and owns source adapters, deny-by-default authorization, customer/tenant checks, sensitive-field allowlisting, SQL retrieval, prompt isolation, citation checks and human escalation. Returns drafts to staff. Only explicit staff approval permits ticket updates; no refund or CRM-write capability. Uses durable approval/idempotency state and reconciliation after ambiguous source responses. Custom implementation required.

data.label: Synthetic ticket queue
data.description: External qualification fixture for ticket ingestion, escalation and approved ticket updates. Its actual API and idempotency/reconciliation contract must be implemented. It is not an IBM managed queue or proof of a production ticket-system integration.

data.label: Existing CRM
data.description: Client-owned CRM, vendor and API unspecified. Application receives read-only access to authorized customer records and allowlists permitted fields before model input. Local qualification uses synthetic CRM fixtures, not live customer records. No customer-record write integration.

data.label: Approved knowledge source
data.description: External source reference; location and API remain unknown. Supplies approved content, source identifiers, revisions and explicit access rules. Content is untrusted input even when approved. Local qualification uses synthetic documents and ACLs.

data.label: Approved knowledge snapshots
data.description: Private IBM Cloud Object Storage for versioned approved knowledge snapshots. Application-managed ingestion records source revision and ACL metadata; read-time approval and authorization checks are required. Retention, encryption and deletion policies remain to be agreed. Broader application integration is not covered by the narrow private-storage generator.

data.label: Authorized catalog and workflow state
data.description: One PostgreSQL deployment stores tenant/customer-scoped knowledge metadata and searchable text, trusted staff mappings, approvals, update outbox, idempotency keys and application audit events. Proposed SQL keyword retrieval filters authorization before selecting content and rechecks revisions before drafting. Transactions and source reconciliation protect retries; database state alone cannot guarantee remote exactly-once updates. Schema, retention and recovery require engineering.

data.label: Grounded draft generation
data.description: IBM watsonx.ai inference candidate. Receives only authorized approved passages and allowlisted customer context; produces a draft with source references or abstention. The application checks references and escalates unsupported promises. Exact model, regional inference, entitlement, API and quality remain unverified. Local scripted responses do not validate a real model.

data.label: Application credentials
data.description: Stores source/API credentials for application retrieval using scoped service access. Keep values outside the diagram and code. Credential provisioning, rotation and Code Engine integration require implementation and verification.

data.label: Redacted operational logs
data.description: IBM Cloud Logs candidate for redacted application diagnostics, authorization denials, correlation IDs, integration failures and escalation events. Durable business approvals and update history live in PostgreSQL. Exclude raw customer fields, prompts and credentials. Routing, access, retention and alert ownership require engineering; ingestion and regional support are unverified.
